Shared1.description: Extension object for platform-specific, vendor-namespaced parameters. Extensions are always optional and must be namespaced under a vendor/platform key (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization.
Shared1.title: Extension Object

cost_per_strengths.description: cost_per strengths supported when combined with max_bid.

roas_strengths.description: roas strengths supported when combined with max_bid.

Shared17.description: Policies supported when budget allocation is fixed or omitted.

Shared18.description: Policies supported when budget_allocation.mode is seller_optimized.

Shared19.description: Standalone policy modes accepted in this exact scope and allocation context. Combination-only components belong only in supported_combinations and need not appear here. `automatic` means the seller accepts and preserves an explicit `{automatic:true}` authored block; omission only invokes inheritance/default behavior.

Shared20.description: Supported standalone cost_per strengths in this profile. Required exactly when modes includes cost_per.

Shared21.description: Supported standalone roas strengths in this profile. Required exactly when modes includes roas.

Shared22.description: Multi-field policies supported in this exact scope and allocation context. Each entry independently qualifies the strengths supported in that combination; standalone strength support does not imply combination support. Absence means no multi-field combination is claimed.

items.description: How a population-level audience-evidence estimate was produced. This vocabulary is intentionally separate from signal-definition methodology: `projected` describes expansion of a sample or panel to a reference population and does not become a user-level signal-membership method.
items.title: Audience Evidence Methodology

Shared9.description: Stable brand identity used to resolve the canonical brand manifest, optionally qualified by the countries of a commercial advertiser entity. The manifest URL is derived from domain; callers do not send brand assets or per-call brand overrides. Countries do not target delivery.

brand_id.description: Brand within a house-of-brands manifest. Omit for a single-brand domain.
brand_id.title: Brand ID

countries.description: Canonical set of ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries for this advertiser identity. Omit when the identity is global or the house does not split the brand geographically. Array order is not meaningful; producers MUST sort codes lexicographically before computing keys or signatures. This qualifies account and proposal identity and is not delivery targeting.

domain.description: Domain that hosts /.well-known/brand.json or is registered for the brand.

Shared9.title: Brand Key

description: Offer, commercial-fit, availability, and reporting filters for product discovery. This compact schema is independent of the legacy delivery-targeting filter graph. Brand and issuer selectors are stable keys; callers do not send brand assets or content provenance.

audience_evidence_requirements.description: Buyer-authored evidence policy for compact product discovery. Organization selectors are stable keys and never carry brand assets or content provenance.

items.description: How subjects were resolved when producing a signal or population-level evidence estimate.
items.title: Audience Resolution Method

items.description: The kind of subject characterized by audience data or population-level evidence.
items.title: Audience Subject Type

allOf.description: A time duration expressed as an interval and unit. Used for frequency cap windows, attribution windows, reach optimization windows, time budgets, and other time-based settings. When unit is 'campaign', interval must be 1 — the window spans the full campaign flight.

interval.description: Number of time units. Must be 1 when unit is 'campaign'.

unit.description: Time unit. 'seconds' for sub-minute precision. 'campaign' spans the full campaign flight.

allOf.title: Duration

audience_evidence_requirements.title: Product Audience Evidence Requirements

items.description: Declared audio distribution classification for radio, streaming-audio, podcast, and other audio inventory, using IAB Tech Lab/OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed definitions with AdCP-native value names. This is seller-declared discovery metadata, not independent verification of inventory quality or delivery context.

enumDescriptions.catch_up_radio: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=4: recorded segment of a radio show that was originally broadcast live.
enumDescriptions.fm_am_broadcast: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=2: FM/AM broadcast, including live content broadcast over the air and also available via online streaming.
enumDescriptions.podcast: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=3: original, pre-recorded content distributed as episodes in a series.
enumDescriptions.text_to_speech: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=7: text-to-speech audio such as audio books or website/plugin article narration.
enumDescriptions.video_game: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=6: background audio in video games.
enumDescriptions.web_radio: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=5: live audio content only available via online streaming, not as FM/AM broadcast.

items.title: Audio Distribution Type

availability_horizon.description: Flexible-window availability discovery: the buyer is open to any bookable window inside [start_time, end_time) and asks the seller to describe when the returned inventory can run, instead of filtering to one exact flight. Sellers that support this field partition the horizon into time-dimensioned forecast rows (forecast-dimension-time) carrying availability_status; sellers that cannot cover the full horizon signal the gap via the response's incomplete[] mechanism. Unlike start_date/end_date this is not an eligibility filter — products remain returnable when only part of the horizon is open. The resulting availability is a snapshot bounded by the forecast's valid_until, never a hold. Mutually exclusive with start_date and end_date, which declare a fixed flight; buyers that already know their dates use those instead.

end_time.description: Exclusive horizon end (RFC 3339 date-time with timezone offset). MUST be after start_time.

start_time.description: Inclusive horizon start (RFC 3339 date-time with timezone offset).

budget_range.description: Extension-tolerant inclusive currency bounds used by legacy discovery filters. At least one bound is required; min MUST be less than or equal to max. The strict negotiation peer that rejects unknown members is media-buy/proposal-budget-constraint.json.
budget_range.title: Budget Range

items.description: Standardized advertising media channels describing how buyers allocate budget. Channels are planning abstractions, not technical substrates. See the Media Channel Taxonomy specification for detailed definitions.

enumDescriptions.affiliate: Affiliate networks, comparison sites, and performance-based partnerships
enumDescriptions.ctv: Connected TV and streaming on television screens
enumDescriptions.display: Digital display advertising (banners, native, rich media) across web and app
enumDescriptions.dooh: Digital out-of-home buying context, including inventory on venue-operated screens and audio players
enumDescriptions.email: Email advertising and sponsored newsletter content
enumDescriptions.olv: Online video advertising outside CTV (pre-roll, outstream, in-app video)
enumDescriptions.print: Newspapers, magazines, and other print publications
enumDescriptions.product_placement: Product placement, branded content, and sponsorship integrations
enumDescriptions.retail_media: Retail media networks and commerce marketplaces (Amazon, Walmart, Instacart)
enumDescriptions.search: Search engine advertising and search networks
enumDescriptions.social: Social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, etc.)
enumDescriptions.sponsored_intelligence: Sponsored Intelligence — advertising within AI assistants, AI search, and generative AI experiences via the reversed data flow
enumDescriptions.streaming_audio: Digital audio streaming services (Spotify, Pandora, etc.)

items.title: Media Channel

countries.description: Filter by country coverage using ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes (e.g., ['US', 'CA', 'GB']). Returns products whose geographic coverage includes at least one of the specified countries. This is a product attribute filter, not a delivery-targeting instruction.

enumDescriptions.non_guaranteed: Inventory without reserved or guaranteed delivery, commonly auction-based or otherwise best-effort. Do not use for scheduled broadcast buys solely because final audience delivery is estimated from historical ranges or settles through third-party measurement.

end_date.description: Fixed-flight availability filter end. See start_date. Mutually exclusive with availability_horizon.

exclusivity.description: Whether a product offers exclusive access to its inventory

enumDescriptions.category: Category-exclusive — only one advertiser per industry category (e.g., one auto brand per collection sponsorship)
enumDescriptions.exclusive: Sole sponsorship — only one advertiser can buy this product
enumDescriptions.none: No exclusivity — multiple advertisers can buy this product simultaneously

exclusivity.title: Exclusivity

items.description: Discriminator naming one of the 15 AdCP 3.2 canonical creative formats, plus `custom` for adopter-defined shapes. AdCP 3.2 adds `audio_vast` for VAST-tag-delivered audio (the standards-conformant profile starts at VAST 4.1, with older versions available only as seller-declared legacy interoperability) and promotes the legacy `multi_state_display` and `multi_placement_takeover` custom shapes to `seller_rendered_stateful_display` and `coordinated_placements`. When `format_kind` is `custom`, the declaration also carries `format_shape` and `format_schema`. The enum mirrors the branches in `product-format-declaration.json` and is closed for producer validation: sellers do not mint ad-hoc values. SDKs may retain unknown future values in tolerant in-memory parsers, but that does not change versioned JSON Schema validation. A seller responding to a 3.1-or-earlier request MUST project away 3.2-only kinds and emit a compatible legacy declaration; a strict older schema correctly rejects an unprojected newer kind. See adcp#3666 and the promotion migration contract in canonical-formats.mdx.
items.title: Canonical Format Kind

items.description: Discriminated reference to a product format option. The global canonical shape is still named by `format_kind`; this reference selects one concrete product `format_options[]` entry. `scope: "publisher"` identifies a publisher-declared catalog option by `{ publisher_domain, format_option_id }`. `scope: "product"` identifies a product-local option by `format_option_id`; the enclosing package/product context supplies the namespace.

oneOf.description: Selects a publisher-catalog-backed product format option by publisher domain and format option ID.

format_option_id.description: Stable format option ID from the publisher's adagents.json top-level `formats[]`, matching a publisher-catalog-backed entry in the target product's `format_options[]`.

publisher_domain.description: Publisher domain where the adagents.json declaring this format option is hosted.

scope.description: Reference resolves against the named publisher's adagents.json top-level `formats[]` catalog.

oneOf.title: Publisher Catalog Format Option Reference

oneOf.description: Selects a product-local format option by ID within the enclosing package/product context. This branch deliberately forbids `publisher_domain` (`publisher_domain: false` in the schema) because product-local references are namespaced by the enclosing product only; include `scope: "publisher"` when the selector must cross into a publisher catalog.

format_option_id.description: Stable format option ID from the target product's inline `format_options[]`.

scope.description: Reference resolves only against the target product's inline `format_options[]`.

oneOf.title: Product-Local Format Option Reference

items.title: Format Option Reference

geo_proximity.description: Inventory coverage in the specified proximity boundaries: OR within this field, AND across offer filters. Does not add delivery targeting, require targeting support, or rescope pricing or forecasts.

geometry.description: Pre-computed GeoJSON geometry defining the proximity boundary. Use when the buyer has already calculated isochrones (via TravelTime, Mapbox, etc.) or has custom boundaries. When geometry is provided, lat/lng are not required.

coordinates.description: GeoJSON coordinates array. For Polygon: array of linear rings. For MultiPolygon: array of polygons.

label.description: Human-readable label for this entry (e.g., 'Düsseldorf', 'Heathrow Airport', 'Primary trade area').

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84). Required for travel_time and radius methods.

lng.description: Longitude in decimal degrees (WGS 84). Required for travel_time and radius methods.

radius.description: Simple radius from the point. The platform draws a circle of this distance around the coordinates.

transport_mode.description: Transportation mode for isochrone calculation. Required when travel_time is provided.

enumDescriptions.cycling: Bicycle travel on roads and cycle paths
enumDescriptions.driving: Motor vehicle travel on road networks
enumDescriptions.public_transport: Public transit including bus, rail, metro, and ferry
enumDescriptions.walking: Pedestrian travel on walkable paths and sidewalks

transport_mode.title: Transport Mode

travel_time.description: Travel time limit for isochrone calculation. The platform resolves this to a geographic boundary based on actual transportation networks.

unit.description: Time unit for isochrone (travel-time catchment) calculations.
unit.title: Travel Time Unit

is_fixed_price.description: Filter fixed-price versus auction offers. Contingent pricing matches neither value.

metros.description: Inventory coverage in the specified metro areas (system and code): OR within this field, AND across offer filters. Does not add delivery targeting, require targeting support, or rescope pricing or forecasts.

code.description: Metro code within the system (e.g., '501' for NYC DMA)

postal_areas.description: Inventory coverage in the specified postal areas: OR within this field, AND across offer filters. Does not add delivery targeting, require targeting support, or rescope pricing or forecasts.

allOf.description: Valid country-local postal system pairing. Registered countries only accept their registered local systems; countries without a registered local system use postal_code or custom.
allOf.title: Postal Country System

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code for the postal values.

values.description: Postal codes within the country and system.

system.description: Deprecated country-fused postal code system (e.g., 'us_zip', 'gb_outward'). Prefer country + postal-system.
system.title: Country-Fused Postal Code System

values.description: Postal codes within the legacy system.

items.description: Postal area values. Prefer the native country + postal system form. Deprecated legacy country-fused postal-system tokens remain accepted for compatibility.
items.title: Postal Area

items.description: How the payable price is determined. Fixed pricing has a seller-declared monetary unit price, auction pricing is established through a buyer bid, and contingent pricing is calculated from a measured business outcome after delivery.

enumDescriptions.auction: Buyer bid against optional floor_price and price_guidance
enumDescriptions.contingent: Price calculated from a measured business outcome after delivery
enumDescriptions.fixed: Seller-declared monetary unit price through fixed_price

items.title: Pricing Structure

property_list.description: Reference to an externally managed property list. When provided, the seller filters products to only those available on properties in the list. This narrows which publisher inventory is returned; it is a product attribute filter, not a delivery-targeting instruction.

agent_url.description: URL of the agent managing the property list

auth_token.description: JWT or other authorization token for accessing the list. Optional if the list is public or caller has implicit access.

list_id.description: Identifier for the property list within the agent

property_list.title: Property List Reference

regions.description: Inventory coverage in the specified ISO 3166-2 subdivisions: OR within this field, AND across offer filters. Does not add delivery targeting, require targeting support, or rescope pricing or forecasts.

allOf.description: Compact seller features relevant to canonical product purchase. Legacy inline-creative capabilities are absent.

scope_capability.description: Support at one authored scope, partitioned by the media buy's resulting allocation mode. Omitted contexts are unsupported; claims in one context make no claim about the other.

bidding_policy.description: Structured declaration of the canonical bidding policies a seller can preserve without semantic translation. Media-buy/package authored scope and fixed/seller-optimized allocation context are advertised independently. Buyers MUST inspect the exact scope, allocation context, mode, strength, and combination rather than treating presence of this object as blanket support.

media_buy.description: Policies accepted at media-buy scope and inherited by packages that omit a package override.

package.description: Policies accepted as package-authored policies, including explicit automatic overrides.

bidding_policy.title: Bidding Policy Capability

reporting_commitment_snapshots.description: Seller preserves the accepted per-purchase reporting contract and exposes it on proposal and MediaBuy readback.

seller_optimized_budget.description: Core seller-optimized shared-budget contract: shared total_budget, seller allocation across packages, media-buy pacing, and allocation echo.

seller_optimized_min_spend_targets.description: Package minimum-spend targets inside seller-optimized buys; implies seller_optimized_budget.

seller_optimized_package_budgets.description: Package budget caps inside seller-optimized buys; implies seller_optimized_budget.

seller_optimized_package_pacing.description: Package pacing inside seller-optimized buys; implies seller_optimized_budget.

allOf.title: Canonical Media Buy Features

required_features.description: Canonical protocol features the seller must support.

items.description: Standard delivery and performance metrics available for reporting. Most values name flat numeric fields of `core/delivery-metrics.json`. Leaf identities address a single numeric value nested inside an object-shaped metric so it can be declared, committed, aggregated, and sorted individually: `quartile_25`/`quartile_50`/`quartile_75`/`quartile_100` resolve to `quartile_data.q1_views`–`q4_views`, and `viewable_rate`/`viewable_impressions`/`measurable_impressions`/`viewed_seconds` resolve to the same-named fields of `viewability`. Structured nested identities `viewed_seconds_percentiles` and `viewed_seconds_histogram` make the corresponding optional distribution carriers discoverable, committable, and requestable, but not aggregatable or sortable. The nested object or array remains the canonical carrier — nested identities never introduce duplicate flat response fields. Container tokens such as `viewability`, `quartile_data`, `dooh_metrics`, and `time_based_views` declare their documented nested surface. **Container subsumption applies only to numeric leaves**: `viewability` subsumes `viewable_rate`, `viewable_impressions`, `measurable_impressions`, and `viewed_seconds`; `quartile_data` subsumes `quartile_25`, `quartile_50`, `quartile_75`, and `quartile_100`. This rule applies to capability declaration, `required_metrics` filtering, format `reported_metrics` intersection, and `requested_metrics` selection. Optional structured identities MUST be declared explicitly: `viewability` alone does not satisfy `viewed_seconds_percentiles` or `viewed_seconds_histogram`. Requesting any nested identity selects its canonical carrier in the response. A nested identity declaration does not imply sibling values or the carrier's non-metric fields.
items.title: Available Metric

metric.description: Performance metrics that support rate thresholds on media buys — the verification subset of the broader metric vocabulary. Each metric specifies whether its threshold is a floor (must exceed) or ceiling (must not exceed). Shared values with `available-metric.json` mirror the delivery vocabulary (`viewability` → `viewable_rate` family, `completion_rate` → same name); verification-only values (`ivt`, `brand_safety`, `attention_score`) are typically vendor-attested and do not appear in `available-metric.json` because they're not seller-reportable scalars — they flow through `vendor_metric_values` or vendor-scope `committed_metrics` entries with the matching `performance_standard.vendor` BrandRef anchoring identity.

enumDescriptions.attention_score: Attention score rate (floor — must exceed threshold). Denominator: measurable_impressions.
enumDescriptions.brand_safety: Brand-safe impression rate (floor — must exceed threshold). Denominator: total_impressions.
enumDescriptions.completion_rate: Video or audio completion rate (floor — must exceed threshold). Denominator: total_impressions.
enumDescriptions.ivt: Invalid Traffic rate (ceiling — must not exceed threshold). Denominator: total_impressions.
enumDescriptions.viewability: Viewable impression rate (floor — must exceed threshold). Requires viewability_standard. Denominator: measurable_impressions.

metric.title: Performance Standard Metric

standard.description: Viewability measurement standard applied to determine whether an impression qualifies as viewable. These are materially different thresholds and should not be compared across standards.

enumDescriptions.groupm: GroupM standard: 100% of pixels in view for 1 continuous second (display) or 50% of video duration.
enumDescriptions.mrc: MRC/IAB standard: 50% of pixels in view for 1 continuous second (display) or 2 continuous seconds (video).

standard.title: Viewability Standard

metric_id.description: Identifier for a vendor-defined metric within the vendor's vocabulary. Stable lookup key; the vendor publishes the canonical list (with category, methodology, and standard alignment) in `brand.json` `agents[type='measurement']`. Lowercase with underscores so a future enum promotion into `available-metric.json` is a literal string lift. Identifier is namespaced by the vendor — the same `metric_id` may mean different things in different vendors' vocabularies.
metric_id.title: Vendor Metric ID

items.description: Declared social-placement surface classification for social inventory, distinguishing the in-app surface where a social placement renders. Values name the semantic surface, not platform brands. This is seller-declared discovery metadata, not independent verification of inventory quality or delivery context.

enumDescriptions.explore: The discovery or browse surface presenting recommended content outside the user's followed graph.
enumDescriptions.feed: The primary scrolling home or timeline surface where posts and ads are interleaved with followed and recommended content.
enumDescriptions.search: The in-app search-results surface, keyed to the user's query.
enumDescriptions.short_video: The full-screen, sound-on, swipe-past, algorithmically-recommended vertical short-video surface. Subsumes the platform brand names for this surface (Reels, Shorts, Spotlight, and TikTok's For You short-video experience) — platform identity belongs to a property/publisher axis, not here.
enumDescriptions.stories: The full-screen, ephemeral tap-through surface presented between or alongside users' story content.

items.title: Social Placement Surface

items.description: Declared sponsored-placement classification for catalog-driven retail-media inventory, distinguishing where the sponsored placement renders on the retailer surface. This is seller-declared discovery metadata, not independent verification of inventory quality or delivery context.

enumDescriptions.sponsored_display: Sponsored placements rendered in display slots across retailer browse, category, and product-detail pages outside the search results stream (e.g., Criteo Sponsored Display, Amazon Sponsored Display on-site).
enumDescriptions.sponsored_native: Sponsored placements rendered using the retailer's native in-grid product template, blending into the organic product listing (e.g., CitrusAd native product cards, Pinterest catalog-driven collections).
enumDescriptions.sponsored_search: Sponsored placements rendered against retailer on-site search results, keyed to the shopper's query (e.g., Amazon Sponsored Products on search, Walmart Connect Sponsored Search).

items.title: Sponsored Placement Type

start_date.description: Fixed-flight availability filter: with end_date, declares the exact flight the buyer intends to run. Returned products MUST be able to serve that flight, and pricing and forecasts are scoped to it. Mutually exclusive with availability_horizon.

items.description: What the publisher wants back from a TMP context match. Determines the richness level of the buyer's offer response.

enumDescriptions.activation: Binary activation with GAM key-values. Offers identify the package via package_id.
enumDescriptions.catalog_items: Preferred catalog items for rendering. Offers may include catalog item references.
enumDescriptions.creative: Inline creative manifest. Offers include full rendering details.
enumDescriptions.deal: Deal ID for programmatic execution. Offers include deal metadata.

items.title: TMP Response Type

items.description: Declared video placement classification for OLV and other video inventory, using the IAB Tech Lab/OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt definitions with AdCP-native value names. This is seller-declared discovery metadata, not independent verification of inventory quality or delivery context.

enumDescriptions.accompanying_content: OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt=2: video ads played with accompanying video content in a player associated with the page or app content.
enumDescriptions.instream: OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt=1: video ads played before, during, or after streaming video content requested by the user.
enumDescriptions.interstitial: OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt=3: video ads shown as an interstitial experience, typically between content or app states.
enumDescriptions.standalone: OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt=4: video ads shown without associated video content, also called no-content or standalone video.

items.title: Video Placement Type
